## Bundled mode (plugin ships and runs the server itself) — v0.4

Goal: someone installs only the plugin from the Marketplace, presses **Open Code Map**, and gets the map of their
project. No clone, no service, no manual Python setup, no LLM, offline.

### Packaging
* The plugin jar contains the Python package and web UI as resources under `/codemap-server/`:
  `codemap-server/codemap/{__init__,__main__,analyzer,server}.py`, `codemap-server/codemap/web/**` (incl. vendor/elk + its LICENSE),
  and `codemap-server/VERSION` (plugin version + short content hash so a changed server re-extracts). No `__pycache__`, no tests.
* Built with **Gradle + IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.x** (`pycharm-plugin/build.gradle.kts`, Gradle wrapper committed),
  which copies `../codemap` into resources at build time, runs `verifyPlugin` (JetBrains Plugin Verifier) and produces a
  Marketplace-ready ZIP via `buildPlugin`. `signPlugin`/`publishPlugin` configured from env vars (CERTIFICATE_CHAIN, PRIVATE_KEY,
  PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD, PUBLISH_TOKEN) but never run by us. IDE dependency: a local IDE via `-PideLocalPath=<dir>` (default: the
  Remote Dev dist on this machine if it exists) else download PyCharm 2025.3. `pycharm-plugin/build.sh` stays as the quick no-Gradle dev
  build and must bundle the same resources.

### Server CLI additions (codemap/__main__.py, codemap/server.py)
* `--port 0` = pick a free port. After binding, print to **stdout** exactly one machine-readable line, flushed:
  `CODEMAP_READY port=<n> url=http://127.0.0.1:<n>/` (other logs go to stderr).
* `--exit-on-stdin-eof`: a daemon thread reads stdin; on EOF the server shuts down cleanly (orphan protection when the IDE dies).
* `--ide-port <n>`: the IDE built-in server port of the owning IDE; `/api/open` tries it first (before probing 63342–63352).
* Must run on **Python 3.10+** on Linux/macOS/Windows, stdlib only (no 3.11+ APIs/syntax; paths via pathlib; no fork-only APIs).

### Plugin: managed server (Java, package dev.codemap.pycharm)
* `CodeMapServerManager` — application-level service (Disposable). `CompletableFuture<String> baseUrl(Project)`:
  - Mode `managed` (default): if a live managed process exists return its URL; else extract resources (if VERSION differs) to
    `PathManager.getSystemPath()/codemap-server/<VERSION>/`, find Python, start
    `<python> -B -m codemap --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0 --exit-on-stdin-eof --ide-port <BuiltInServerManager port>`
    with working dir = extracted dir (so `-m codemap` resolves) and `PYTHONPATH` = extracted dir, `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`;
    parse `CODEMAP_READY` from stdout (timeout 20 s); forward stderr to idea.log (Logger). One process per IDE, shared by all projects.
    Restart automatically on next request if it died. Destroy on dispose (IDE exit).
  - Mode `external`: use the configured URL as-is (power users / the old systemd service).
  - Never runs on the EDT.
* Python discovery (first that reports version >= 3.10 via `-c "import sys;print('%d.%d'%sys.version_info[:2])"`, 5 s timeout):
  settings override path → project SDK home (`ProjectRootManager.getProjectSdk().getHomePath()`) → module SDKs →
  PATH: `python3`, `python`, and on Windows `py -3`. Uses only platform APIs (no Python-plugin dependency).
  Failure → clear message listing what was tried.
* Tab UX: the Code Map tab opens immediately with a "Starting Code Map…" page (JCEF `loadHTML`), then navigates to
  `<base>open?root=<project dir>[#focus=…]` when ready. On failure shows an error page with the reason, what was tried, and a
  Retry button + link to Settings. URLs from actions are built against the base URL once known.
* Settings (Tools | Code Map): Server mode [Bundled (automatic) | External URL] + URL field, Python interpreter override (optional,
  blank = auto), read-only status line (running on port N with python X / not running), "Restart server" button.
* Plugin id stays `dev.codemap.pycharm` for now (vendor/id to be finalised before first Marketplace upload).
EOF

content.text:
The bundled version is being built now; I'll report back when it finishes.

**What's being built:**
- **Python service inside the plugin.** The plugin unpacks it on first use. It then finds a Python 3.10 or newer, checking in order: a path you set yourself, the project's interpreter, then `python3`/`python` (or `py` on Windows). It starts the service on a free port.
- **One service per PyCharm session.** All open projects share it, and it shuts down when PyCharm closes. If PyCharm crashes, the service exits by itself.
- **Better tab behaviour.** The tab opens at once with a "Starting Code Map…" page. If something fails, such as no suitable Python, it shows the reason and a Retry button instead of a blank page.
- **Settings.** Bundled (automatic) is the default. You can still point at an external service, override the Python path, see the service's status, and restart it.
- **Marketplace-ready build** with JetBrains' Gradle tooling, their compatibility checker, and a `PUBLISHING.md` step-by-step guide.

**How it's checked:** the build is tested as if on a brand-new machine: empty plugin data and only Python 3.10 available, plus a case with no Python at all. Two independent reviews then go through it: one walks through it as a new user on Windows, macOS and Linux, the other checks threading, leftover processes and safety.

**Still open:** the plugin ID and vendor name for the Marketplace. Once a plugin is published, its ID can't change, so decide on a name like `com.tourteller.codemap` (or your own) before the first upload.

- `/home/sushil/PycharmProjects/codemap/codemap/server.py`
  - `serve()` prints one stdout line right after binding, then flushes: `CODEMAP_READY port=<n> url=http://127.0.0.1:<n>/`. The two messages that used to go to stdout, plus "shutting down" and a new "stopped", now go to stderr. Note this also applies to your systemd service; journald still captures them.
  - `--exit-on-stdin-eof`: a background thread reads stdin and shuts the server down cleanly when stdin closes. It also works when stdin is closed from the start.
  - The SIGTERM handler is now installed before the socket is bound, and everything after binding is inside the shutdown block. Before this, a SIGTERM sent right after the READY line killed the process with a traceback instead of a clean exit.
  - `--ide-port`: when opening a file in the IDE, the given port is tried first, then 63342–63352.
  - Windows fixes:
    - Port reuse (`SO_REUSEADDR`) is now POSIX-only. On Windows it lets a second server take a port that's already in use.
    - The `/mnt/<drive>/` launcher check only runs on Linux.
    - The `pycharm` launcher is started detached in a Windows-safe way.
    - `pycharm64` was added to the launcher names it looks for.
    - Project ids ignore case on Windows (so `C:\Proj` and `c:\proj` are one project). Ids on Linux are unchanged.
- `/home/sushil/PycharmProjects/codemap/codemap/__main__.py`: the new options, and Windows' error code 10048 is now recognised as "port already in use".
- `/home/sushil/PycharmProjects/codemap/codemap/analyzer.py`: no changes needed. Its paths are already posix-style, it uses nothing newer than 3.10, and its output on gis_api is identical on 3.10 and 3.12 (1469 nodes, 1884 edges).

  - Copies the package to a temp dir and starts `python -B -m codemap --port 0 --exit-on-stdin-eof --ide-port …` the way the plugin will.
  - Checks the READY line format, then `/open?root=<fixture>` → 302 → `/p/<id>/api/graph` contains `pkg/a.py`.
  - Closes stdin and requires exit code 0 within 3 s, with nothing else on stdout.
  - Also covers: without the option, closing stdin doesn't stop the server; the IDE port is tried first and the scan falls back to the range when it's dead; project-id format and case handling.
- `/home/sushil/PycharmProjects/codemap/tests/test_server.py`: the WSL launcher test now only expects a match on Linux.
- `/home/sushil/PycharmProjects/codemap/README.md`: the new options, the READY line, and a paragraph on bundled mode.

Nothing was tested inside a running IDE yet: the tab, the settings page, the JCEF pages and `CodeMapServerManager` itself compiled but were never exercised.

**Files changed** (all under `/home/sushil/PycharmProjects/codemap/pycharm-plugin/`)
- New `src/main/java/dev/codemap/pycharm/ServerLauncher.java`: the pure logic, with no IntelliJ imports. It covers Python version and `CODEMAP_READY` parsing, ordering the Python candidates, probing them (5 s timeout), reading `VERSION` from a classloader, extraction and launching. Extraction lists the files from the jar, or from an unpacked directory, or from a `codemap-server/FILES` list. It writes to a temp dir and moves it into place in one step, writes `VERSION` last so only complete copies count, and deletes other version dirs. Launching keeps stdin open, waits for READY (20 s), sends server output to a log callback, and on failure reports the exit code plus the last stderr lines. Shutdown closes stdin, then calls destroy, then force-kills if needed. There is also a `join(base, target)` helper for URLs.
- New `src/main/java/dev/codemap/pycharm/CodeMapServerManager.java`: the application service, registered in `plugin.xml`.
  - `baseUrl(Project)` returns a `CompletableFuture`, and all projects share one start in progress.
  - It finds Python in this order: settings override, then the project SDK and module SDKs (Python SDKs only, remote ones skipped), then `python3`, `python` and on Windows `py -3`. PATH comes from `EnvironmentUtil`.

- `CodeMapPanel.java`:
  - The tab opens at once with a "Starting Code Map…" page; the base URL is resolved off the EDT, then the project map loads.
  - On failure it shows an error page with the reason and Retry / Open Settings buttons (through a second `JBCefJSQuery`), plus a Swing bar with the same buttons above the browser.
  - A failed page load (e.g. the server died) shows the same error page. Retry keeps the current `#focus` and restarts the server.

**Per finding**

The stdin thread always calls the shutdown hook, which stops the server and exits with `os._exit(0)` if shutdown takes more than 1 s. The plugin now carries its own copy of the Code Map service, so it works with nothing else installed. Version 0.4.0 is installed as `com.sushil.codemap`, vendor Sushil, and is ready for the Marketplace. Restart PyCharm (File → Exit, then reconnect) to load it.

**What someone who downloads it gets:** they press Open Code Map (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+K) and the tab shows "Starting Code Map…", then their project's map. Behind that, the plugin:
- unpacks the service the first time it's used;
- finds a Python 3.10 or newer: a path you set, then the project's interpreter, then whatever is on PATH, including Homebrew and python.org installs on macOS and `py` on Windows;
- starts one shared service on a free port, which stops when PyCharm closes, or within half a second if PyCharm crashes.

If no suitable Python is found, the tab says what it tried and offers Retry or Open Settings.

**Tested:**
- **Clean install:** a brand-new install with only Python 3.10 available started in under a second, mapped `gis_api` with all 1,469 functions and classes, and shut down cleanly with nothing left running. With no Python at all, the expected error page appeared.
- **JetBrains' compatibility checker:** reports Compatible against PyCharm 2025.3, with no internal or deprecated API use.
- **Python tests:** all 45 pass on 3.10 and 3.12.
- **Reviews:** two independent reviews found 13 issues, and all are fixed. The serious one: if PyCharm was force-killed, the service kept running forever.

**Not tested yet:**
- **Inside PyCharm:** the tab, the starting and error pages, and the settings page compile but haven't run in a live PyCharm. That happens on your restart. If anything looks off, tell me what you see.
- **Windows and macOS:** handled in the code, but not run on a real machine.

**Large projects:** on a project of about 3,000 files, every save re-analyses everything, taking about 20 seconds and around 1.4 GB of memory. The first open shows an "Analysing…" page instead of hanging. Re-analysing only changed files would fix this, and I'd do it before a public release.

**Your settings:** they were reset by the ID change, so after the restart the plugin uses its own bundled service. The always-on background service I set up earlier on port 8765 is no longer needed. Should I remove it?

**Publishing:** `pycharm-plugin/PUBLISHING.md` has the steps. The file to upload first is `pycharm-plugin/build/distributions/codemap-pycharm-0.4.0.zip`. After that first manual upload, `./gradlew publishPlugin` handles updates with a token.

lastPrompt: instead of using python, why are we not using java itself to do the indexing and analyzing. Just curious.

content.text:
Mostly because of how this started, not because Python is the better choice for a plugin. Your first request was a standalone web service, and Python's built-in parser was the quickest accurate way to read Python code. The plugin was added on top of that. For a Marketplace plugin, doing the analysis in Java inside PyCharm would be the stronger design.

**Why Python made sense at first:**
- **Exact parsing:** Python's built-in parser always understands the code exactly as Python does, including new syntax.
- **Works anywhere:** the service runs without an IDE, from a browser, a terminal, or other editors.
- **Fast to build** and easy to test.

**What a Java version would gain.** It wouldn't need its own parser: it would use PyCharm's own model of your code, the one behind Ctrl+click, Find Usages and refactoring.
- **No Python requirement.** The interpreter search, unpacking and background process all go away. Nothing to start, so nothing can fail to start.
- **Far better accuracy.** PyCharm already works out types, including library types. Many of the calls my analyzer currently lists as unresolved, about 70% of all calls, would become real links. For example, `db.execute(...)` would link to SQLAlchemy's `Session.execute`.
- **Instant updates on big projects.** PyCharm already re-reads only the file you changed, so the map could update just that part. That fixes the roughly 20-second full re-analysis on large repos.
- **Less to maintain.** The plugin could serve the web page itself, so there's no separate port or background process to manage.

**What it would cost:**
- **Tied to PyCharm.** It would only work in PyCharm, or IntelliJ with the Python plugin, and the standalone browser mode would go away unless we keep the Python version alongside it.
- **Version churn.** It would depend on PyCharm's Python plugin interfaces, which change more between releases than the general IDE interfaces the plugin uses now.
- **Waits for indexing.** It can't run until PyCharm finishes indexing the project.
- **Heavier testing.** Tests would need JetBrains' IDE test framework instead of quick Python tests.

Writing our own Python parser in Java would be the worst of both: a lot of work, and it would fall behind new Python syntax.

**Recommendation:** for the Marketplace version, move to PyCharm's own model. The map, the left-to-right layout and the graph data format stay exactly the same; only the part that produces the graph gets replaced. The Python version could stay as an optional standalone tool. It's a sizable change, but contained, and it also solves the big-repo performance problem. Want me to plan it out?
